questions.q: When was the Constitution of India adopted?
questions.e: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India on 26 November 1949, which is why this date is celebrated as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas).

questions.q: When did the Constitution come into force?
questions.e: The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day, chosen to honour the 1930 Purna Swaraj declaration.

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee?
questions.e: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly, which was responsible for preparing the draft Constitution.

questions.q: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar is known as the:
o: Chief Architect of the Indian Constitution
questions.e: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar is widely known as the Chief Architect (or Father) of the Indian Constitution for his central role in drafting it.

questions.q: How many Articles were there in the original Constitution?
questions.e: The original Constitution of India contained 395 Articles divided into 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.

questions.q: How many Parts did the original Constitution contain?
questions.e: The original Constitution was organised into 22 Parts, though amendments have since added more Parts (such as Part IXA and IXB).

questions.q: How many Schedules were there originally?
questions.e: The original Constitution had 8 Schedules; amendments over time have increased this number to 12.

questions.q: At present, the Constitution contains approximately:
questions.e: Due to numerous amendments, the Constitution now has approximately 470 Articles, 25 Parts, and 12 Schedules.
The Preamble describes India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic — 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976).

questions.q: Which of the following is guaranteed by the Constitution?
questions.e: The Constitution provides for Fundamental Rights (Part III), Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV), and Fundamental Duties (Part IVA) — all three together.
